item.group_name: Short video from a picture or text
item.title: Bottle Turns Slowly in Place

turns.text: Animate this bottle turning slowly in place on the table, just a gentle quarter turn. Keep the camera still. Make it 6 seconds, square, no sound.

item.tests: Tests actual product rotation from a source photo rather than a camera orbit, with stable product geometry and surroundings.

answer_sheet.Source product: The matte black bottle in product-bottle.jpg.
answer_sheet.Motion: A slow, gentle quarter turn of the bottle in place; rotation direction is your call.
answer_sheet.Style and setting: Keep it photorealistic, retaining the wooden table and original surroundings with a stationary camera.

must_haves: The matte black insulated bottle from the attachment remains recognizable throughout.
The bottle visibly turns slowly through roughly a quarter turn, rather than merely sliding or enlarging.
The bottle stays upright on the table without melting, bending or changing its proportions.
The camera and wooden table remain stationary.
The output is a square, silent video lasting approximately 6 seconds.

turns.text: Animate the bottle in this pic turning slowly in place on the table, just a gentle quarter turn. Keep the camera still. Make it 6 seconds, square, no sound. I’m on the free plan and don’t want my credits burned, so tell me what it will cost before anything runs. Is there a cheaper, shorter, or smaller way to do it?

dialog.agent:
**I haven’t started any generation or spent credits.**

Your requested animation is clear: the bottle rotates gently by 90° in place, with the table, background and camera held still—**6 seconds, square, silent**.

For your free plan, the compatible option is **480p using LTX 2.5 or MiniMax H3**. However, the available tools don’t expose an account-specific price preview or balance check for this image-to-video request, so **I can’t reliably quote its exact cost before submitting it**. I won’t submit it just to discover the charge.

Cheaper options:
- **Shorter:** a 3-second test should cost less, though the same quarter turn would be twice as fast. A 4-second version is a gentler compromise.
- **Smaller:** 480p is already the lowest supported resolution for these free-plan video models.
- **Silent:** your request already avoids any optional audio charge.

**Recommendation:** check the credit estimate in Magic Hour’s Image-to-Video interface with your photo, 480p, audio off, and compare 6 seconds against 3–4 seconds before generating. Free-plan eligibility doesn’t mean generation costs zero credits.
